references.text: Isaiah prophesies about a future where the wolf shall dwell with the lamb – a contrast to Jesus' image of disciples as lambs among wolves.
Ezekiel is sent to a rebellious people, paralleling how Jesus sends out his disciples into a potentially hostile environment.
Jesus uses exactly the same image when he sends out the twelve: 'Behold, I send you out as sheep among wolves.' This is the closest parallel to Luke 10:3.
Jesus speaks of the wolf that comes and scatters the flock – the same imagery of sheep/lambs and wolves as in the sending of the seventy.
Paul warns that 'ravenous wolves' will come into the church – the same imagery of wolves threatening the flock.
Jesus warns against false prophets who come in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves – the same wolf-sheep metaphor.
Benjamin is described as a wolf that tears in pieces – an early example of the wolf as a symbol of hostility and danger, which provides background for Jesus' metaphor.
